newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Mark volatilities up as dlr/mark rallies.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Mark volatilities up as dlr/mark rallies.

text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar/mark and mark/yen options rose in European morning trade as the mark weakened broadly against major currencies.
Dollar/mark vols firmed across the curve, with one-month at 9.35/9.60 percent at 1105 GMT against 8.90/9.10 in Europe late on Monday and one-year at 9.45/9.75 percent versus 9.35/9.55.
Traders said, however, that activity had begun to cool down somewhat since the spot dollar hit its highs overnight.
"There's been a slowdown in dollar/yen volatilities, which has been leading the dollar/mark," said one options trader at a German bank here.
"(In the spot market) dollar/mark is now taking the lead, but with dollar/yen reined in, maybe it's time to start getting some profit-taking in dollar/mark," the trader said.
Dollar/mark hit a high of 1.7350 overnight, though it had edged down to 1.7326/36 by Europe's midday.
Dollar/yen vols were mostly stable, with one-month at 9.20/9.50 percent against Monday's 9.20/9.70.

Risk reversals in both major pairs favoured the U.S. unit, traders said. One-month dollar/mark risk reversals were quoted at 0.35/0.55 percent for dollar calls, with dollar/yen was similarly skewed at 0.2/0.5 percent.
Volatilities in mark/yen options firmed as the mark's overall weakness pulled it down against the Japanese currency.

One-month mark/yen vol was trading at 7.90/8.15 percent, up from Monday's 7.70/8.00, while one-year vols stood at 8.35/8.65 versus 8.30/8.60. Mark puts were in vogue, with one-month risk reversals quoted at 0.2/0.5 percent.
"Mark/yen vols have been better bid purely on the fact that spot mark/yen fell below 73, although admittedly there hasn't been massive trading in options this morning," the German bank trader said.

Sterling/mark vols edged lower, ignoring the pound's continued rally which took it to a fresh 4-1/2-year high of 2.8215 marks this morning. One-month sterling/mark vol dropped to 9.20/9.60 percent from Monday's 9.40/9.70 and risk reversals were bid for pound calls at 0.15/0.45 percent.
